items.text: Flight restrictions against Iranian airplanes have expanded in the region. After Iraq, Oman, and Azerbaijan, the UAE and Turkmenistan have also denied entry or passage to Iranian airplanes. All flights of Iranian airlines to the UAE have been canceled.

Iran and Middle East developments were main topics in leaders' speeches at the UN General Assembly. Key points included reopening the Strait of Hormuz, freedom of navigation, and Iran's nuclear program. More details were provided by Ali Rashid.

The Saudi Civil Defense Organization warned of a renewed attempt to attack Mecca. The warning was initially issued and then canceled. Additionally, six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis were intercepted and destroyed.

Reports from Dastgerd prison in Isfahan indicate worsening health conditions and the spread of diseases such as meningitis. Several prisoners have been transferred to hospitals and visitations have been restricted. There is also widespread infestation of lice, fleas, and ticks, along with shortages of medicine and medical services.

According to information received by Iran International, all flights of Iranian airlines to the United Arab Emirates have been cancelled. These flights were operating from cities including Tehran, Kish, Mashhad and Shiraz. The cancellation follows the implementation of US restrictions on the foreign activities of Iranian airlines, and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had previously announced that these activities would be halted from the first of Mehr.

Iranian rowers won gold, silver, and bronze medals at the Nagoya 2026 Asian Games rowing competitions. Fatemeh Mojallal won two medals, gold and bronze, while Amirhossein Mahmoudpour won a silver medal. This report was provided by Alireza Modiri for Iran International.

The morning flight on Thursday, October 2, by Varash Airlines from Tehran to Dushanbe was forced to return to Khomeini Airport after not receiving overflight permission from Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan. This occurred due to new US sanctions and increased flight restrictions in the region. The flight was consequently canceled.

Yahya Rahim Safavi stated that the Yemeni Houthis have made significant progress in weapon production. He also mentioned that the connection of the Persian Gulf, Red Sea, and the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab will change the battlefield. Ahmad Vahidi supported Masoud Pezeshkian's speech at the UN and said Iran is not afraid of war.

Sasan Zamani, 36 years old and resident of Kerman, was sentenced to five and a half years in prison. He was tried on charges including assembly and collusion to commit crimes against national security and propaganda activities against the regime. Zamani was arrested on January 10 in Kerman.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, welcomed Xi Jinping, the President of China, and his wife at Andrews Air Force Base. The visit is scheduled for three days, and a red carpet was laid out for the ceremony. The reactions of Trump and Xi to the passage of a B-1 bomber during the US national anthem attracted attention.

Oksana Chusovitina, a 51-year-old Uzbek gymnast, reached the vault final in her seventh Asian Games appearance and finished seventh. She has participated in eight Olympic Games and aims to compete in the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. Chusovitina has had one of the most unique careers in gymnastics.

The Iranian women's lightweight double sculls team won the first team gold medal for Iranian women's rowing at the Nagoya Asian Games. Solmaz Abbasi explained the importance of these medals and the difficult training conditions for female rowers.

Delsy Rodriguez stated that Venezuela has entered a new phase after political and natural crises. She thanked the US for its readiness to resume diplomatic relations with Venezuela. Rodriguez expressed the desire to maintain cooperative and respectful relations with the international community.

Hassan Taftian advanced to the semi-finals of the 100-meter dash at the Nagoya Asian Games with a time of 10.46 seconds. Fatemeh Mohitizadeh also topped the standings on the first day of the heptathlon.

Reza Shafakhah, the lawyer of Amirhossein Mousavi, announced that his client was tried in Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of moharebeh and corruption on earth. These charges can lead to severe sentences, including the death penalty. The third session of Mousavi's trial was held on Monday, 30 Shahrivar.
A number of Iranians living in Germany gathered in Hamburg at the start of the new school year. They commemorated the students killed in Iran. They read out the names of these students.

Donald Trump stated during his meeting with the Chinese president that they have developed an excellent friendship and made significant progress in bilateral relations. He mentioned plans to discuss security, technology, and artificial intelligence with Xi Jinping. The two countries are also working towards more balanced trade relations, including new market access for American farmers and ranchers.

The interrogation session of Ali Kalateh Dolati, a detainee related to the December 2025 protests, was held on Sunday, September 29, at the seventh investigative branch of Sabzevar Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office. He was charged with propaganda against the regime and defended himself. Ali Kalateh Dolati is imprisoned in Sabzevar prison.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the President of Iran, will be interviewed today at 6 PM Eastern Time by Bret Baier on Fox News. The interview will be at 1:30 AM Tehran time on Friday. The exact time and network for the interview have been announced.

Xi Jinping met with Donald Trump at the White House and said China and the US have a responsibility to cooperate for human progress. He emphasized honest dialogue and increasing mutual trust, noting broad areas for cooperation. Xi also called for healthy competition and avoiding conflict.

Najmeh Amini, a prisoner sentenced to death, is held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. She has been sentenced to death and over 12 years in prison in two separate cases. The charges include blasphemy, acting against national security, and propaganda against the regime.

Ehsan Hajsafi reached 149 national team appearances in a friendly match against Uzbekistan, equaling Javad Nekounam's record. He also captained the team in this game. In the 10th minute, he made a mistaken pass that led to Uzbekistan's first goal.

Abbas Araghchi met with the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Ukraine, and Poland on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly. The Pakistani Foreign Ministry stated that they discussed bilateral relations and regional developments. Araghchi and the Ukrainian foreign minister emphasized the importance of diplomacy in managing tensions.

The fifth Iran Conference, hosted by the Nofdi Institute, is underway in Washington. The topics of this two-day meeting include US policy towards the Islamic Republic, the future of negotiations, Iran's nuclear program and military capability, and sanctions.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International complaining about paying 400,000 tomans for a package of biscuits and two packages of chips and puffed snacks, most of which were filled with air. This issue was raised as a complaint about the price and quality of the packages. The video was sent to Iran International.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said reactions to the meeting of Western officials with Islamic Republic authorities should be broader and hold Western politicians accountable for what he called double standards on human rights. He emphasized that in the context of reports of crimes against humanity in Iran, dialogue with Islamic Republic officials without considering these issues is questionable.

Miad Maleki, former head of the sanctions targeting office at the US Treasury, said that restricting flights of Iranian airlines by regional countries is to protect airports and private companies. This measure is taken to shield them from the consequences of sanctions.

Abdulrahman Abdollahi-Pour, a member of the Hana Human Rights Organization, was detained in Turkey and transferred to a foreign nationals' detention center. The organization warned that returning him to Iran could lead to arrest, torture, and even the death penalty. Hana has called on Turkey to halt his deportation and ensure his access to a lawyer.

The Iranian national football team lost 3-1 to Uzbekistan in their first match after the 2026 World Cup. This was Iran's first preparatory match before the 2027 Asian Championship. Sardar Azmoun played for one half after months of absence, and Denis Derghahi was also in the lineup.

The director of disability prevention and social integration at the Welfare Organization reported ongoing problems for children with disabilities in rural areas accessing education. Causes of school dropout include poverty, lack of trained teachers, and transportation issues. These barriers remain especially in less privileged areas.

More than 300,000 dahlia flower heads were used to create a 29-meter artwork in Bradford's Centenary Square. The piece was designed by Shiraz Ali, a local artist. This is the first British version of the "Flower Carpet," an event regularly held in Belgium since the 1970s.

Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife arrived in the US to speak at the UN General Assembly. He will stay in New York for less than eight hours before returning to Israel. Netanyahu will meet with nine world leaders, five of whom are from Latin American countries.

A father married off his eight-year-old daughter due to financial problems. This event is an example of child marriage and a violation of children's rights. No further information about the man's age or the location has been released.

Iran ranked sixth in the medal table at the end of the fifth day of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya with 12 medals, including 3 gold, 6 silver, and 1 bronze. Gold medals were won in rowing and wushu. China, Japan, South Korea, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan are the top five teams in the table.

Mohammad Shehbaz Sharif, Prime Minister of Pakistan, met with Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Abbas Araghchi, Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Khawaja Muhammad Asif, and Tariq Fatemi also attended the meeting. The discussions focused on bilateral relations and regional developments.

A citizen sent a video showing pollution from the Dorud cement factory. The Lorestan Environmental Protection Organization confirmed the factory is outdated and its pollution has increased. The factory produces about 900,000 tons annually.

Abbas Araghchi had brief and informal meetings with foreign ministers of several countries on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. These meetings included ministers from Jordan, Tajikistan, Armenia, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Poland, Ukraine, Lebanon, and the Prince of Brunei. The news was announced by Abbas Araghchi's Telegram channel.

Joachim Wadtfol, Germany's foreign minister, stated that any negotiation with Tehran must end the nuclear threat posed by the Islamic Republic and expressed doubt about Iran's willingness to abandon its nuclear program. He emphasized the importance of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and rejected Iran's collection of tolls there. Wadtfol also condemned the Houthis in Yemen and announced Germany's support for Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government.

Mohammad Naderi, a prisoner in Tehran's Great Prison, was sentenced to death for espionage by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. This sentence was reported by the HRANA news agency. Naderi was arrested during security developments related to the war.

The Israeli government launched an advertising campaign against Iran's nuclear program in New York ahead of the speeches by Israeli and Palestinian leaders at the UN General Assembly. Messages such as "Nuclear Iran is a threat to the entire world" were displayed on 500 digital billboards and 12 trucks in Times Square and Manhattan. The cost of this advertising was paid by the Israeli government.

Babak Khatami, a pediatrician, stated that sanctions are not the sole cause of drug shortages and cited factors like budget deficits and drug distribution structure. He warned of an impending silent crisis in Iran's health sector. He also emphasized the need for transparency and international oversight.

Xi Jinping, the President of China, supported the return of the US and Iran to the Islamabad agreement. He urged both countries to quickly return to resolving issues through negotiation. Earlier, Xi Jinping emphasized the responsibility of both countries for the progress of humanity in a meeting with Donald Trump.
The program with Kambiz Hosseini will not be aired tonight due to live coverage of the UN General Assembly in New York. The next program will be on Monday, Mehr 6, at 11 PM Tehran time.

Iran International has revealed aspects of the humanitarian crisis in the Dastgerd and Dowlatabad prisons in Isfahan. Issues such as the spread of contagious diseases, denial of medical treatment, and physical and psychological torture have been reported. The media outlet has invited people to share their information and experiences about the prisoners' conditions.

A military training camp for pro-government forces has been established in Imam Hossein Square in Tehran. This move coincides with increased security measures and militarization of public spaces, including schools. Videos published on social media show this development.

Antonio Costa, President of the European Council, asked the Islamic Republic to stop attacks on neighboring countries. He also called for full freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and resumption of cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency. These statements were made during a meeting with Masoud Pezeshkian.

Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Israeli Army, stated that the Israeli military is monitoring developments in the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces. He said the Iranian regime is wounded but has failed to change its intentions. Additionally, the entry of the submarine 'Dragon' into Israel's fleet has enhanced the operational capabilities of the navy.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated at the UN General Assembly that he prevented Iran from obtaining a nuclear bomb. He described destroying Iran's nuclear facilities as one of the easiest decisions of his premiership. Netanyahu also said that even secretly, they are thanked for this action.
Benjamin Netanyahu spoke about confronting the Islamic Republic of Iran in his speech at the United Nations. He also mentioned the death of Ali Khamenei. He began his remarks with the topic of Iran.

Younes Bakri, Yaser Havasizadeh, and Rouhollah Gholami, three citizens from Asmanabad, remain in detention. Parts of their video confessions during detention were broadcast on Ilam provincial network. The conditions under which these confessions were obtained and their judicial status are unclear.

The Israeli Prime Minister said at the UN General Assembly that Israel did not collapse after the October 7 attack and fought on seven fronts. He identified Hamas, Hezbollah, Houthis, the Islamic Republic, and Palestinian armed groups as the fronts and said they were defeated. Netanyahu also stated that the missile threat against Israeli civilians has ended and Hezbollah leaders have been killed.

The One Million Signatures campaign started in 2006 to change discriminatory laws in Iran and challenged legal inequalities. This movement became widespread with the participation of women, men, and support from over fifty civil organizations. Although it faced restrictions after 2009, its intellectual and social achievements remain.

Netanyahu gave a speech at the United Nations, which received positive reactions from the Iranian people. Some Iranians referred to him as the only true representative of the Iranian people at the UN and called for the destruction of the IRGC. Criticisms were also made regarding the diplomacy of other countries towards the Islamic Republic.

Workers at Saipa Large Industrial Molds Company in Tehran went on strike due to unmet demands. Additionally, 42 workers at Mahan Company in Moltan village, Mehrestan county, protested low wages and unpaid salaries by striking. These strikes are related to labor protests in these two areas.

The Israeli Prime Minister said at the UN General Assembly that Israel is engaged in a media war in addition to a military one. He accused Qatar of financially supporting universities and media against Israel and accused Turkey of supporting Hamas and other actions. Netanyahu emphasized that Israel will stand against the global campaign of misinformation.

The Israeli Prime Minister at the UN General Assembly accused Qatar of hosting perpetrators of the October 7 Hamas attack. He also accused Turkey and Erdogan of supporting terrorism and illegal actions. Netanyahu referred to Turkey's occupation of Northern Cyprus and its threats against Israel.

The Israeli Prime Minister said at the UN General Assembly that the Islamic Republic fears the Iranian people and restricts freedom of expression through internet censorship. He described the Starlink device as a symbol of free access to information and called for it to be made available to the Iranian people. Netanyahu also criticized the global silence on human rights violations in Iran and predicted the regime's downfall was near.

The Israeli Prime Minister met with the Prime Ministers of Greece and Slovenia on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The meeting with the Greek Prime Minister emphasized the importance of strategic partnership for regional stability. Greece's selection of Israeli defense systems was also welcomed.

In September 1405, 47 deaths due to lack of workplace safety and 172 worker injuries were recorded. Additionally, 146 gatherings and seven worker strikes were reported. These statistics indicate ongoing job insecurity and livelihood problems for workers.

The Israeli Prime Minister rejected the genocide accusation against Israel at the UN General Assembly, calling it the biggest lie of this century. He emphasized that the Israeli army has made significant efforts to reduce civilian casualties. Netanyahu also accused the New York mayor of promoting anti-Semitism.

Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, responded to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte's remarks about five thousand sorties from European bases supporting the US attack. He stated this shows Europe was part of the infrastructure for the attack. Gharibabadi warned that governments allowing US use of their territory bear responsibility and this cooperation will not go unanswered.

Videos received by Iran International show that Iranians and Ukrainians held protests in London in front of the Russian embassy. These protests coincided with Iranians worldwide supporting the national revolution. Iranians carried images of Prince Reza Pahlavi during the demonstrations.

Benjamin Netanyahu criticized protesters and officials who left the hall during his speech at the UN General Assembly. He questioned why there is silence regarding the massacre of tens of thousands of unarmed Iranian civilians. Netanyahu referred to human rights violations by the Islamic Republic.

The Canadian government announced a new round of sanctions against officials and institutions of the Islamic Republic. The Canadian Prime Minister described the Islamic Republic as a major threat to the world and Israel. This report was published by Mahsa Mortazavi from Iran International.

Iranian wushu athletes won one gold and three silver medals in the sanda category on the fifth day of the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games. This information was shared by Jalil Ataei, bronze medalist of the 2006 Asian Games.

Najat Bahrami said the lobbying capacity of supporters of the Iranian people and Prince Reza Pahlavi in the US has not yet reached full influence. Nofodi plays an important role in conveying the demands of the Iranian people to American policymakers. The formation of these networks started relatively late due to the increasing demand for the overthrow of the Islamic Republic.

The national football teams of Germany and the Netherlands drew 1-1 in their first UEFA Nations League match. Felix Nmecha scored for the Netherlands, and Akpa Akpro equalized in the 92nd minute. Xavi Hernandez did not lose in his first experience as the Netherlands coach.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Tehran seeks to revive the ceasefire agreement with the US before the November midterm elections. He said Iran does not want the issue to reach the elections and wants the Americans to return to the agreement beforehand. These remarks came as contacts between Iran and the US increased during the UN General Assembly.

Benjamin Netanyahu said at the UN General Assembly that the rulers of the Islamic Republic fear the Iranian people above all. He criticized Western countries' silence regarding the killing of Iranian civilians. Netanyahu predicted that the Islamic Republic will be overthrown and the Iranian people will achieve freedom.

Cristiano Ronaldo played in Portugal's first match under coach Jorge Jesus against Wales but his goal was disallowed for offside. He was substituted in the 67th minute and handed the captain's armband to Bruno Fernandes.

Kambiz Tavana said the Iran issue could become part of broader Washington-Beijing talks on topics like Taiwan and North Korea. Iran's position, especially with China's role in oil purchases and Strait of Hormuz developments, affects Tehran's bargaining power. The main priority of both countries remains economic issues and trade competition, with regional topics discussed within this framework.

Netanyahu stated that the rulers of Tehran fear the Iranian people more than anything else. These remarks were made in the audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad. The topic relates to political concerns in Iran.

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, offered a Starlink satellite internet device to Iranian diplomat Nasser Asadi at the UN General Assembly. Asadi did not accept or acknowledge the device. The device had been previously introduced by Benjamin Netanyahu to help Iranians bypass internet censorship.

Turkey and Iraq agreed on the gradual transfer of the Bashiqa military base to the Iraqi government after their leaders met in New York. This base has been a major point of dispute for over a decade. They also emphasized the return of Iraqi sovereignty over the Sinjar region and the end of illegal foreign armed groups there.

The Kuwaiti Crown Prince accused the Islamic Republic of carrying out missile and drone attacks against Kuwait and GCC countries as well as Jordan. He described these attacks as violations of international law and the UN Charter, targeting civilian infrastructure. He also accused Iran of disrupting shipping and using the Strait of Hormuz as a bargaining tool.

Abdullah Abdulqadir Al-Alimi, deputy head of Yemen's leadership council, accused the Houthis of rejecting the Saudi and Omani peace roadmap and escalating tensions in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab to serve Iran's goals. He said these actions have turned one of the world's most important waterways into a tool of pressure. He also emphasized that protecting Bab al-Mandab is a shared regional and international responsibility.

Luis Montenegro, the Prime Minister of Portugal, condemned the actions of the Iranian government and its affiliated groups in his speech at the United Nations. He called for an end to attacks on neighboring countries, commercial ships, and civilian facilities, as well as the lifting of the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. He also described the protection of seas and freedom of navigation as a shared responsibility requiring collective cooperation.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that everyone in Iran has the right to protest but described the December protests as a coup attempt. He announced the death toll as three thousand and apologized for mismanagement. He also said that the instructions come from Mojtaba Khamenei and the government implements them.

Colombia announced it has cut diplomatic relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran as of September 19, 2026. The reasons include security concerns, alleged ties between Tehran and terrorist groups, human rights violations, and Iran's actions in the region. Consular relations between the two countries will continue.

The "NIAC" group has sued US President Donald Trump for continuing the war with the Iranian government without congressional authorization. The group has asked the federal court to declare this action unconstitutional. NIAC states that the authority to declare war under the US Constitution rests with Congress, and Trump has continued the war with Iran without obtaining such authorization.

About 80 countries issued a joint statement calling for the immediate and full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and condemned attacks by Iran and the Houthis. The statement was read by Bahrain's foreign minister at the United Nations. The signatories emphasized the safe passage of ships through this waterway.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan will hold an emergency meeting with their military commanders to discuss support for Riyadh following attacks by Yemen's Houthis. The meeting aims to review support for Riyadh's right to self-defense within the framework of a joint defense agreement. Analysts have expressed doubts about the implementation and commitment levels of the Makkah Pact.

Israeli officials believe that resuming attacks on Iran is only a matter of time and Israel is prepared defensively and offensively. They threatened to attack nuclear facilities if Tehran crosses red lines. Additionally, Israeli elections will not affect the decision for a possible attack, and the ongoing US-Iran negotiations are considered insignificant.

Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that Iran has never sought nuclear weapons and adheres to the framework of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. Responding to a question about 60% uranium enrichment, he stated that Iran is ready to dilute these materials and attributes the problem to US behavior. Pezeshkian also emphasized that Iran will continue to resist despite economic problems caused by sanctions and will not surrender.

Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran has made a proposal to the US that could lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the resumption of negotiations for a final agreement. The proposal was presented to Washington through intermediaries, and the US must implement specific conditions within seven days. The details of the conditions were not disclosed but are said to be more than the terms of the Islamabad agreement.

Dani Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, offered Naser Asadi, the representative of the Islamic Republic, a Starlink device in a video and suggested he take it to Tehran. He said the device could be useful in Iran and help the Iranian people achieve freedom. Danon also expressed hope for regime change in Iran.

The Russian Foreign Ministry announced that Sergey Lavrov and Abbas Araghchi emphasized the necessity of a diplomatic resolution to the crisis caused by the US and Israel's war against Iran during their meeting in New York. The ministry called the actions of the US and Israel illegal and stated there is no alternative to a diplomatic solution. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2025 that foresees closer defense cooperation.

Masoud Pezeshkian has expressed readiness to inspect nuclear facilities and address the issue of 60% uranium reserves. He and Abbas Araghchi tried to show in New York that the Islamic Republic is ready for agreement and cooperation. Pezeshkian did not give a clear answer about guaranteeing military forces' adherence to the potential agreement.

Mohammad Motamedizadeh, a member of the Presidium of the Parliament's Article 90 Commission, announced in an interview with the Khaneh Mellat news agency on Friday, the 3rd of Mehr that if US threats continue, withdrawing from the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) could be put on the agenda. He described these threats as a sign of the other side's desperation. He also emphasized that one should not show weakness in the face of threats.

The Islamic Republic has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for reducing or lifting the naval blockade. Kamyar Behrang says this waterway is no longer an effective leverage in negotiations with the US. The Strait of Hormuz issue has become a global crisis, with pressure from various countries to reopen it.

Shayan Samiei stated that the Houthi attacks on Saudi oil export routes aim to prevent Saudi Arabia from using an alternative safe route. These attacks increase risk, insurance costs, and ship rental fees. The Houthis want to increase pressure on Saudi Arabia regarding finding an alternative oil export route.

Fatemeh Mohitizadeh, Iran's heptathlon representative at the Nagoya Asian Games, was disqualified for wearing non-standard shoes after competing in six events and holding second place overall. Only one event remained, and she likely could have medaled. She had achieved top ranks in several events including the 100-meter hurdles and high jump.

Hanieh Rostamian and Vahid Golkhandan won the bronze medal in the mixed pistol event at the Nagoya Asian Games with 415 points. The Indian team took first place with 484 points, and South Korea came second with 478 points.

Mehdi Saremi Far emphasized the importance of free internet and Starlink for the people of Iran. He stated that the Islamic Republic has used communication shutdowns as a tool for repression. Starlink cannot fully replace Iran's internet but helps people maintain their connections.

Masoud Pezeshkian held a meeting on the evening of October 2 in New York with several prominent figures in American media and think tanks. Attendees included Robert Malley and Trita Parsi. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

The management of Najaf Airport announced the suspension of all incoming flights from Iran and outgoing flights to Iran from 2 AM Friday until further notice. This decision was made based on official orders from relevant authorities. The Iranian Civil Aviation Organization also announced the suspension of accepting flights of Iranian airlines at Baghdad Airport.

On the third day of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, Benjamin Netanyahu emphasized the collapse of the Islamic Republic of Iran. He stated that the ruling regime in Iran fears its people more than anything else. This report was provided by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.

Abbas Araghchi stated in a meeting with the Portuguese foreign minister that insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is a result of actions by the US and Israel. He called for stopping unsafe actions by the US to restore maritime security. He also urged the European Union to adopt an independent and responsible approach to regional developments.

Hossein Abdi resigned as head coach of Iran's U23 football team after returning to Iran. The team was eliminated in the group stage of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya. Abdi accepted responsibility for the results and apologized to the Iranian people.

A court session was held for nine women residing in Ahvaz at the Revolutionary Court of the city. They are accused of membership in opposition groups, propaganda against the regime, and conspiracy against internal or external security. The judge sentenced each to five years in prison, with a reduction to one year if they complete a mandatory ideological reform period.

Iranians in Germany held a rally on Friday, September 25, in support of Ali Zarei in front of the US Embassy in Dusseldorf. Ali Zarei is a protester of the Mahsa movement and a prisoner in Iran facing the risk of execution. The demonstrators demanded action to prevent his execution.

The police commander of Yazd province announced the arrest of a woman in the province. She is accused of involvement in the arson of a mosque in Tehran and disturbing public order during last December's protests. This information was reported by Harana News Agency.

Morteza Nemati, the Nagoya Asian Games champion, admitted to pretending to have a mental disorder to get a military exemption. He said after returning to Iran that he obtained a psychiatric exemption in the past year. Nemati did this to participate in national team camps and acknowledges that his action was wrong.

A citizen reported in a video that water was continuously cut off for 33 hours. Due to the depletion of water reserves, he faced difficulties in bathing and cleaning his shop. The citizen addressed Masoud Pezeshkian and asked if the United States had cut the water.

A viewer of Iran International said Masoud Pezeshkian's speech does not matter to them, and they consider the speeches of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu more important. The viewer identified Reza Pahlavi as the true representative of the Iranian people. They hope Reza Pahlavi will attend international assemblies as the official representative of the Iranian nation.

Hamid Ghaeni-Nejad, a resident of Mashhad, remains in indefinite detention in Vakilabad prison after six months. He suffers from physical problems and requires continuous medical care but has been deprived of proper treatment. Forensic medicine has confirmed his inability to endure imprisonment, and a one billion toman bail has been set, which he cannot afford.

A citizen in Shiraz spray-painted an image of Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi on a wall. Next to the image, a famous verse from Shahnameh and slogans "Long live Iran" and "Long live the Shah" were written. This video was published by Iran International.

Rouhollah Rahimpour spoke about China's role in Tehran-Washington negotiations, stating that Beijing can play a significant mediating role. He added that this role cannot be considered decisive. China has relations and economic interests with both sides.

Mohsen Mahyemini from Iran International said many viewers considered Benjamin Netanyahu the voice of the Iranian people in the world after his speech. Some viewers also hope that Prince Reza Pahlavi will attend next year's General Assembly meeting.

Iranian representatives won silver and bronze medals in gymnastics, rowing, and shooting at the Asian Games. Fatemeh Mohitizadeh was disqualified from athletics for using unauthorized shoes. More details were reported by Alireza Modiri.

The Iranian men's 3x3 basketball team defeated the Philippines 21-10 in the bronze medal match at the Nagoya Asian Games. The players included Mohammad Ghaffari, Basir Momeni, Sarem Jafari, and Mohammad-Mehdi Rahimi. Iran lost 14-11 to Qatar in the semifinals.

Security forces used live ammunition, shotguns, and deadly weapons to suppress protests in Kurdistan, Kermanshah, and West Azerbaijan. These actions have been reported in these regions. Protests continue in these provinces.

Amir Safari's family and children held a birthday ceremony at his grave in Behesht Zahra on the first of Mehr. A dove was released in memory of him during the ceremony. Amir Safari was killed on January 9, 2026, in the Sattarkhan neighborhood of Tehran at the age of 48.

The Left Party of Germany, after winning the Berlin elections, intends to invite the Green Party and the Social Democrats to preliminary coalition talks. The Green and Social Democratic parties have conditioned the start of negotiations on an agreement to protect the lives of Jewish citizens. The Left Party will vote on the official invitation at its congress.

Donald Trump and Xi Jinping emphasized maintaining stability and expanding cooperation. Despite disagreements on issues like trade and Taiwan, the two countries must interact. China prefers to play a mediating role regarding the Islamic Republic.

The Iranian U23 football team returned to Tehran after a 4-1 loss to North Korea and elimination from the group stage of the Nagoya Asian Games. Esmaeil Gholizadeh apologized to the public and cited infrastructure issues and last-minute player additions as reasons for the defeat. He denied rumors of player negligence and expressed hope for the future.

Saeed Shirali, 22 years old, was killed on the evening of January 8 during protests on Azadi Street in Tehran by government forces. His mother said she searched for him for three days and found his body with three bullet wounds.

Families of political prisoners executed in 1988 were prevented from entering Khavaran Cemetery today and placed their flowers behind closed gates. They held a ceremony at the site to honor the victims. Security forces filmed the families at the end of the ceremony.

Mohammad Mokhber reacted to the suspension of Iranian airlines' flights in some countries and threatened those countries. He stated that flights in the region should be free for everyone or for no one. He also said that if Iran cannot fly or receive airport services, no country in the region will have this possibility either.

Amnesty International launched a global campaign to end impunity for perpetrators of crimes against humanity in Iran, coinciding with the release of a report on the crackdown on the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising. The organization has called on people to sign a petition urging UN member states to establish an international mechanism to investigate and prosecute those responsible.

Iran's men's and women's national kabaddi teams advanced to the final of the Nagoya Asian Games by winning their semifinals. The women's team defeated Taiwan 23-19, and the men's team won 59-21. Both teams will face India in the final.

Mohammad Saeedi called unveiling hijab religiously and politically forbidden and demanded action against women who do not observe hijab. He emphasized that those unaware should be dealt with through education and awareness. He also stated that those who deliberately threaten national security must face legal and security measures.

The Italian Council of Ministers approved a plan to ban the burqa, masks, and face-covering garments that prevent full identification of students in schools. Violations of these regulations will be fined up to one thousand euros. This news was reported by Sadaf Baghbani.

In Bojnord, mosques and Hosseiniyehs were used to deploy forces and organize plainclothes agents. One Hosseiniyeh was turned into a gathering place for plainclothes forces. Surveillance cameras were also used to identify protesters.

The Israeli Prime Minister accused Recep Tayyip Erdogan of being responsible for the killing of thousands of Kurdish civilians at the UN General Assembly. He also criticized the Turkish government for suppressing the Kurds. These statements were made in Benjamin Netanyahu's speech.

Pezhman Amani from Saqez and Shahin Mostafazadeh from Mahabad were arrested separately by intelligence agents on Wednesday, 1 Mehr. They were transferred to an unknown location. Pezhman Amani's and his family members' phones were also confiscated.

The Amitt Institute for Terrorism and Intelligence Research reported an increase in the role of Chinese parts in the Houthi's military capabilities. The institute stated that China has become one of the main sources for supplying drone parts and weapons to the Houthis. This report is based on data from intercepted shipments.
The Australian national team scored first in the 68th minute with a goal by Nestori Iranconda. Brazil equalized in the 90+5th minute with a goal by Ryan. The match ended in a draw.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh stated that regional countries previously sought an agreement to permanently limit Iran's nuclear and missile threats. He added that with increased US sanctions and naval and air blockades, the situation has changed. Regional countries now prefer to continue pressure until Iran accepts the conditions of the US and the region.

Pakistan's Foreign Ministry announced that under the Makkah joint defense agreement, an attack on any member is considered an attack on all members. The foreign ministers of the three countries met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and condemned attacks on Saudi Arabia. They also discussed holding an urgent meeting of military chiefs and establishing the agreement's secretariat.

Benjamin Netanyahu's plane passed through Canadian airspace en route to New York for a UN General Assembly speech. Canada had previously stated it would enforce the ICC arrest warrant if Netanyahu entered its territory. A Canadian foreign ministry spokesperson said the overflight permission does not imply endorsement of Israeli policies and was granted due to the importance of diplomatic interactions.

With new US sanctions against Iran's aviation industry, flight restrictions for Iranian companies in the region have increased. Flights from Iran to Najaf, Erbil, and Sulaymaniyah have been stopped. Access to other routes has also faced limitations.

The mother of Amir Setarirad participated in the memorial campaign by lighting a candle at his grave. Amir Setarirad was an environmental researcher and teacher who was killed on January 9, 2026, in Karaj. His mother expressed the absence of her son in the classroom.

Masoud Pezeshkian rejected the published statistics about the casualties of the December protests in an interview with Fox News. He stated that the number of casualties was slightly more than three thousand. These remarks were made in an interview with Samira Gharaei, a reporter for Iran International.

Two emergency medical experts in Shiraz were attacked with a cold weapon by individuals under the influence of drugs and alcohol during a mission. One expert has been discharged from the hospital, while the other underwent surgery due to lung injury. The condition of the second expert is reported as stable.

David Perdue, the US ambassador to China, stated that Trump told Xi Jinping that any direct or indirect Chinese support to Iran is unacceptable. Washington is concerned about indirect Chinese support for Iran but lacks direct evidence. Trump and Xi are working on building a relationship based on trust.

At the start of the school year, images of mothers who have abandoned mandatory hijab and daughters who are still required to wear the headscarf have widely circulated on social media. Ayah Dris, a member of Iran International's editorial team, has explained these reactions.

Nawaf Salam, the Prime Minister of Lebanon, called for a new chapter in Tehran-Beirut relations during a meeting with Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. He emphasized that Lebanon does not want to become a field for regional conflicts or message exchanges. This meeting took place on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

Iran and Middle East war developments were key topics in the UN General Assembly speeches. Some officials emphasized stopping attacks and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. This was mentioned in reference to actions by the Islamic Republic and allied groups.
